# Refinement log — C6

*Generated by `layer2_clinical/11_refinement_loop.py`. This log, not the performance change, is the deliverable for C6 (SPEC.md §4.7).*

## Design

- Set B scoreable: 830 patients, split once with seed 42 into 645 diagnosis / 185 final holdout.
- The holdout was scored **exactly once**, after the refinement was fixed.
- Refinement rules were written down before any diagnosis ran, so the choice of refinement could not be steered by the holdout.

## Round 1 — predictions confronted with outcomes

Trained on set A (n=3198), predicted on the set B diagnosis slice (n=645).

- Enrichment: 25.0% event rate in predicted-positive vs 18.2% in predicted-negative (RR 1.377, p=0.0428)

## Refinement decisions, each traced to its trigger

| Rule | Fired | Observation that triggered it | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | YES | predicted-positive prevalence 36.0% on B vs 27.0% on A, gap 9.0% | threshold moved 0.5 -> 0.845 to match A's prevalence |
| R2 | YES | risk ratio 0.118 in sparse vs 1.708 in complete patients, gap 1.59 | added measured-variable count as an explicit feature |
| R3 | no | all features available in >=50% of set B | — |


## Round 2 — evaluated on the final holdout

| Round | n | RR | AUC | event rate (pos) | event rate (neg) | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (baseline) | 185 | 1.622 | 0.6336 | 22.8% | 14.1% | 0.1997 |
| 2 (refined) | 185 | 2.024 | 0.629 | 27.3% | 13.5% | 0.0393 |


**Delta: risk ratio +0.402, AUC -0.0046.**

**Mixed, and the distinction matters.** Enrichment improved (risk ratio 1.622 -> 2.024) while discrimination did not (AUC 0.6336 -> 0.629). Both refinements act on the OPERATING POINT — a threshold move cannot change ranking at all, and AUC is threshold-invariant — so this is the expected shape rather than a contradiction. The deployable quantity got better; the model did not. Reporting only the risk ratio would overstate what happened.

## What this loop cannot do

- Set B has no endotype labels (D15), so the loop optimises **enrichment quality** against sepsis onset rather than agreement with a reference assignment. That is the deployable objective, but it is not the same objective the round-1 model was trained for.
- One cycle only. A second cycle would need a second holdout.
